page: Amazon Web Services d3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. Compute is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 dedicated physical cores with multithreading. Memory allocation is 32 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, giving an 8 GB memory ratio per physical core. Storage is provisioned via 5,940 GB of integrated local hard disk drive (HDD) capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included.

Benchmark results characterize the instance by its modest compute profile relative to its storage capacity. The stress-ng suite recorded 1324.19 for single-core and 3488.06 for multi-core compute throughput, placing CPU performance in the lower benchmark quartiles. Geekbench testing returned a single-core score of 1124.0 and a multi-core score of 2464.0, while PassMark registered an overall CPU score of 4112.43 alongside an average memory tier score of 2126.68. The instance sustained 3.45 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.78 GB/sec in static web throughput.

The hardware configuration trades high compute velocity and random I/O performance for high local magnetic storage volume. This profile provides clear cost efficiency for sequential read and write operations on large data footprints that do not require solid-state latencies. Appropriate workloads include distributed storage clusters, data lakes, Apache Hadoop or MapReduce storage nodes, log aggregation, and sequential data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services d3.xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor delivering 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by 32 GB of DDR4 system memory. Its primary operational differentiator is the inclusion of 5,940 GB of bundled local HDD storage, supported by a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps without integrated GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks place its raw processing performance in the lower tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core rating of 2464.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 4112.43, alongside a balanced PassMark memory score of 2126.68. The hardware allocation delivers substantial storage density per vCPU at the expense of compute intensity and high-IOPS capabilities. This setup fits large-capacity sequential data workloads, such as distributed file systems, centralized log archives, batch analytical processing, and MapReduce storage nodes.
